The parent allocation is freed exactly once, only after its successful allocation. The separately allocated child is never freed. Ordinary successful live malloc allocations do not overlap; the single parent free is not a child free or repeated release.

If both ordinary malloc calls succeed, two distinct allocations exist. The only pointer to the child is stored in the parent's ptr field. free(a) releases only the parent, losing that child pointer without releasing the child. At function end exactly the child obligation remains; the parent contributes no expected leak. Failed parent allocation returns immediately; failed child allocation acquires no child obligation.
